How do you pronounce: L-A-B-I-S-S-I-E-R-E ?|url=http://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/video/pop-quiz-how-do-you-pronounce-l-b-i-s-s-i-e-r-e|editor=Press|publisher=NBC Sports|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=March 5, 2018}} born March 18, 1996) is a Haitian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He graduated from [[Lausanne Collegiate School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]],{{cite web|title=Skal Labissière, draft #1 NBA 100 % haïtien|url=http://lenouvelliste.com/lenouvelliste/article/143806/Skal-Labissiere-draft-1-NBA-100-haitien|website=LeNouvelliste.com|date=April 20, 2015|access-date=June 4, 2015|language=fr}} before playing one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He played for the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] before being signed to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for one year. ==Early years== Labissière was born in [[Port-au-Prince]] in [[Haiti]]. His basketball career began at the [[Collège Canado-Haïtien]], a junior-senior high school in [[Port-au-Prince]], which participated in school championships organized by the {{not a typo|Comité Interscolaire de Basket-ball Amateur}} (CIBA) and the {{not a typo|Association de Basket-ball Interscolaire}} (ASI). During the [[2010 Haiti earthquake]], his family's home collapsed with Labissière, his mother and his brother inside. All three survived but remained trapped under debris for three hours. His legs were pinned, causing them to go numb, and Labissière was unable to walk for a few weeks after. A few months following the earthquake, Labissière moved to [[Memphis, Tennessee]], to live with Gerald Hamilton, who ran the Reach Your Dream Foundation that brings international athletes to the United States as young prospects.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Remsberg|url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/7448728/skal-labissiere-survived-2010-haiti-earthquake|title=Rise Above: Skal Labissiere|work=ESPN.com|date=January 14, 2012|access-date=August 22, 2014}}{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Roberts|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2013/01/31/2498350/kentucky-target-labissiere-a-walking.html|title=Kentucky target Labissiere a walking, shooting 'miracle'|work=Kentucky.com|date=January 31, 2013|access-date=March 25, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Parrish|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/19614399/after-surviving-haitis-quake-labissiere-out-to-make-most-of-his-second-chance|title=After surviving Haiti's quake, Labissiere out to make most of his second chance|work=CBSSports.com|date=July 19, 2012|access-date=August 22, 2014|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414022629/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/19614399/after-surviving-haitis-quake-labissiere-out-to-make-most-of-his-second-chance|archive-date=April 14, 2016}} ==High school career== Labissière attended [[Evangelical Christian School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]] and started to play varsity basketball as an eighth-grader. When he had first arrived, Labissière spoke little English and required a [[French language|French]] interpreter in all of his classes. After three to four months, he didn't need the help and became fluent. In 2014, he left the school his senior year and enrolled at [[Lausanne Collegiate School]], also located in Memphis,{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Smith|url=http://archive.commercialappeal.com/sports/preps/skal-labissiere-enrolls-at-lausanne-but-apparently-wont-play-basketball-ad-says-ep-570598641-324345041.html|title=Skal Labissiere enrolls at Lausanne, but apparently won't play basketball, AD says|work=CommercialAppeal.com|date=August 22, 2014|access-date=August 22, 2014}} but because of the move he was ruled by [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association|TSSAA]] as ineligible to play basketball at Lausanne for the season. Instead, Labissière played for Hamilton's Reach Your Dream Prep Academy team, where he averaged 26 points, 12 rebounds and 4.5 blocks per game.{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Jones|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/kentucky/2015/01/10/labissiere-improves-despite-playing-losing-team/21575397/|title=UK signee Labissiere improves on losing team|work=Courier-Journal.com|date=January 11, 2015|access-date=June 3, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Norlander|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24772263/the-strange-high-school-setup-for-five-star-prospect-skal-labissiere|title=The strange high school setup for five-star prospect Skal Labissiere|work=CBSSports.com|date=October 28, 2014|access-date=June 3, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Dauster|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/28/skal-labissiere-reach-your-dreams-prep-and-why-this-isnt-as-scuzzy-as-it-sounds/|title=Skal Labissiere, Reach Your Dreams Prep and why this isn't as scuzzy as it sounds|work=NBCSports.com|date=October 26, 2014|access-date=June 3, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Jones|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2015/05/09/super-five-skal-labissiere/27054767/|title=2015 Super Five - Rivals.com|work=Rivals.com|access-date=November 12, 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/142888/skal-labissiere|title=Skal Labissiere - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profile|work=ESPN.com|access-date=November 12, 2016}} He committed to the [[University of Kentucky]] (UK) to play [[college basketball]].{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Cohen|url=http://archive.commercialappeal.com/sports/skal-labissiere-picks-kentucky-over-memphis-other-finalists-ep-768655596-324299551.html|title=Skal Labissiere picks Kentucky over Memphis, other finalists|work=CommercialAppeal.com|date=November 13, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014}}{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Cohen|url=http://archive.commercialappeal.com/sports/skal-labissiere-signs-with-kentucky-praises-guardians-ep-770275480-324299171.html|title=Skal Labissiere signs with Kentucky, praises guardians|work=CommercialAppeal.com|date=November 14, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014}}{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/11871615/skal-labissiere-isaiah-briscoe-commit-kentucky-wildcats|title=Kentucky gains 2015's top class|work=ESPN.com|date=November 14, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014}} UK's coach, [[John Calipari]], offered Labissière a scholarship before any other 2015 prospect, comparing him to [[Anthony Davis]]. At the start of the season, he was considered a potential number 1 draft pick for the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Wasserman|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2560713-ben-simmons-or-skal-labissiere-who-starts-year-as-nba-drafts-no-1-prospect|title=Ben Simmons or Skal Labissiere: Who Starts Year as NBA Draft's No. 1 Prospect?|work=BleacherReport.com|date=September 8, 2015|access-date=September 8, 2015}} Labissière posted averages of 6.6 points (.516 FG%, .661 FT%), 3.1 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 15.8 minutes per game in all 36 games while starting 18 of them for the [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/skal-labissiere-1.html|title=Skal Labissiere College Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=November 12, 2016}} On April 5, 2016, Labissière declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nba-draft-2016-freshman-skal-labissiere-is-a-boom-or-bust-prospect/|title=NBA Draft 2016: Freshman Skal Labissiere is a boom or bust prospect|work=CBSSports.com|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 5, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2016–2019)=== On June 23, 2016, Labissière was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 28th overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft, becoming the highest drafted Haitian player since [[Samuel Dalembert]] (26th overall in [[2001 NBA draft|2001]]). His rights were later traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on draft night,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-draft-night-trade|title=Kings Announce Draft-Night Trade|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}} and on July 15, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Kings.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-papagiannis-richardson-labissiere|title=Kings Sign Papagiannis, Richardson and Labissiere|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}} Labissière made his NBA debut on November 5, recording eight points and three rebounds in 15 minutes off the bench in a 117–91 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899535|title=Kings vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2016|access-date=February 24, 2017}} On February 23, 2017, in just his ninth game of the season, Labissière had a season-high 12 points in a 116–100 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900261|title=Cauley-Stein scores 29, Kings beat Nuggets 116-100|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}} On March 1, in his first career start, Labissière had 10 points and five rebounds in 15 minutes in a 109–100 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899448|title=Nets end 16-game skid with 109-100 road win over Kings|work=ESPN.com|date=March 1, 2017|access-date=March 2, 2017}} On March 15, he scored 21 of his career-high 32 points in the fourth quarter of the Kings' 107–101 win over [[2016–17 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]], becoming the first rookie from the 2016 draft class to score at least 30.{{cite web|last=Khan|first=Shahbaz|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/labissieres-career-night|title=Labissiere's Career Night|work=NBA.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}} He also had 11 rebounds to record his first career double-double.{{cite web|last=Tagle|first=Benedict|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/recap-kings-suns-31517|title=Labissiere, Kings Outshine Suns in Phoenix|work=NBA.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}} Labissière became the youngest Kings player to record a 30–10 game and the fourth Kings player to do it as a reserves since the 1984–85 season.{{cite web|last=Khan|first=Shahbaz|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/career-night-puts-rookie-rare-company|title=Career Night Puts Rookie in Rare Company|work=NBA.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} His points total was the highest for a Kings first-year player since teammate [[Ben McLemore]] scored 31 in 2013–14. Labissière became only the 41st player in NBA history to score at least 32 points while age 20 or younger—the only other player to achieve this feat in franchise history is [[Tyreke Evans]]. During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On December 5, 2017, Labissière was assigned to the Reno Bighorns.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-skal-labissiere-assigned-to-g-league/|title=Kings' Skal Labissiere: Assigned to G-League|work=cbssports.com|date=December 5, 2017|access-date=January 22, 2018}} He was recalled by the Kings four days later.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-skal-labissiere-back-from-reno/|title=Kings' Skal Labissiere: Back from Reno|work=cbssports.com|date=December 9, 2017|access-date=January 22, 2018}} On January 2, 2018, Labissière recorded 17 points and a career-best 15 rebounds in a 131–111 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975298|title=Howard, Walker help Hornets pull away and beat Kings 131-111|work=ESPN.com|date=January 2, 2018|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On January 22, he scored a season-high 23 points in a 112–107 loss to the [[2017–18 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975433|title=Walker, Lamb lead Hornets past Kings 112-107|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2018|access-date=January 22, 2018}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2020)=== On February 7, 2019, Labissière was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Caleb Swanigan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2019/2/7/blazers-acquire-skal-labissiere|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Skal Labissière|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}} On April 10, Labissière started the season finale for Portland as the team was resting its rotation players for the playoffs. In 40 minutes of action, Labissière had 29 points and 15 rebounds, helping the Blazers overcome a 28-point deficit in a 136–131 win. On February 6, 2020, Labissière and cash considerations were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for a future protected second-round draft pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/2/6/blazers-complete-trade-with-atlanta-hawks|title=Trail Blazers Complete Trade with Atlanta Hawks |work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020}} He did not play any games for the Hawks and at the end of the season, he did not re-sign with the team either, and became a free agent.{{cite web |last1=Spencer |first1=Sarah K. |title=Bembry, Labissiere among four Hawks becoming free agents |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/jones-bembry-labissiere-brown-to-become-unrestricted-free-agents/J2FHDSC6FREQDKHEU2MJCNHOIM/ |website=ajc.com |access-date=December 6, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}} ===Westchester Knicks (2021)=== On December 9, 2020, Labissière signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Skal Labissière |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-skal-labissiere |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 10, 2020 |date=December 9, 2020}} He was waived two days later.{{cite tweet |user=NY_KnicksPR |number=1337508553960153092 |date=December 11, 2020 |title=New York Knicks announced today that the team has waived center/forward Skal Labissière.}}{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Colin |title=Knicks waive C/F Skal Labissiere, roster now at 19 players |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/knicks-waive-c-f-skal-215348928.html |website=sports.yahoo.com |access-date=December 12, 2020 |date=December 11, 2020 |archive-date=May 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503130349/https://sports.yahoo.com/knicks-waive-c-f-skal-215348928.html |url-status=dead }} He was then added to the Knicks’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Westchester Knicks]]. He made his Westchester debut on February 10, 2021. ===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2022)=== Labissière joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs 2021 MGM Resorts NBA Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2021/vegas/team/1610612759/spurs|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 17, 2022}} On March 10, 2022, Labissière signed with [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Skal Labissiere joins Cangrejeros de Santurce|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/skal-labissiere-joins-cangrejeros-de-santurce/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=March 10, 2022|access-date=March 11, 2022}} ===Mexico City Capitanes (2023)=== On March 3, 2023, Labissière was acquired by the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2023}} On April 26, 2023, Labissière signed with [[Grises de Humacao]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican league]],{{cite tweet|number=1651312761320751108|title=OFICIAL: El centro Skal Labissiere es el nuevo refuerzo de los Grises de Humacao en sustitución de Thomas Robinson.|user=LaGuerraBSN|author=La Guerra del BSN|date=April 26, 2023|access-date=June 9, 2023|language=Spanish}} but didn't play for them. ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2023–2025)=== On September 8, 2023, Labissière signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] and was waived the same day.{{cite tweet|first=Keith|last=Smith|title=The Sacramento Kings have waived Skal Labissiere, as part of a process to get Labissière to the Stockton Kings of the G League. This sign-and-waive plan for Sacramento and Labissiere was first reported by @James_HamNBA.|number=1700681932911120677|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=September 9, 2023|access-date=September 9, 2023}} On November 9, Labissière was named to the Opening Night roster for the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2023-24 Opening Night Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2023-24-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} On September 26, 2024, Labissière re-signed with Sacramento,{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Skal Labissière|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-skal-labissiere|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} but was waived on October 18.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-roster-moves-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} On October 27, he joined the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} On March 3, 2025, Sacramento signed Labissière to a 10-day contract.{{cite web | title=Kings Sign Skal Labissière to 10-Day Contract | website=NBA | date=2025-03-03 | url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-skal-labissiere-to-10-day-contract | access-date=2025-12-10}} In four appearances for the Kings, Labissière averaged 1.3 points, 0.8 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2025–2026)=== On October 6, 2025, Labissière signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Washington Wizards]], but was waived seven days later. He was then added to the Wizards' G League affiliate, the [[Capital City Go-Go]]. On January 27, 2026, Labissière signed a 10-day contract with the Wizards.{{Cite web|title=Washington Signs Skal Labissiere to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washington-signs-skal-labissiere-to-10-day-contract|access-date=January 27, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
